source: Native AWS Lambda SigV4 REST/JSON and AWS CLI IAM/STS

context.method: One immutable base role policy; each condition is an STS inline session policy with identical Action/Resource/Effect. No role policy mutations during measurements. Each actual session is measured in a first pass after all sessions for its matrix are issued, and again at an age of at least 30 seconds, with no-condition controls before and after each matrix. Root means authorized probe caller, not AWS root user. Request writes reset Case/case to before-upper/before-lower and root ListTags records before/after every measured write. IAM internal context is not observable: only submitted tag maps, policies and outcomes are evidence.
context.redaction: Account normalized to 000000000000; credentials/access-key IDs/signatures/session tokens never retained. STS assumed-role ARN and principal ID retained. No code download URLs requested.
context.wire_serialization: Signed body uses Python json.dumps(body,separators=(comma,colon)) with sort_keys=False; input.body member order is the actual wire JSON order. SigV4 canonical header sorting does not sort JSON members. Mixed-case supplement additionally stores wire_body_utf8. Canonical URI double-encodes the percent-encoded resource ARN; prior_attempts retains the initial incorrect-signature attempt and complete cleanup without interpreting it as an IAM outcome.

documentation.finding: Condition key names are case-insensitive; case-distinct resource tag keys can produce unexpected condition failures when only one value matches.

ResourceTag and RequestTag classified single-valued; AWS advises not using set operators on them. TagKeys is multivalued. Captured set-operator behavior is empirical, not recommended policy construction.
StringEquals compares values case-sensitively. ForAllValues requires every context value to match; ForAnyValue requires at least one. Negated set operators are captured separately.

supplemental_mixed_case_controls.source: Native AWS Lambda SigV4 REST/JSON and AWS CLI IAM/STS

context.method: Own separate function and roles, unchanged scoped base role policy, immutable session policies differing only in the condition. Twelve sessions vary ResourceTag/RequestTag key spelling Case/CASE/case and StringEquals upper/lower. Same sessions compare reversed and forward tag-map insertion orders, then swapped value bindings. Three successful no-condition controls separated by 10 seconds precede measurements; no-condition ListTags succeeds after every scenario. Root ListTags records all resource maps and every request write before/after. Inputs retain original JSON member order; mixed-case run also records exact signed UTF-8 body. Root means authorized probe caller, not AWS root user.
context.redaction: Account normalized to 000000000000; credentials/access-key IDs/signatures/session tokens never retained. STS assumed-role ARN and principal ID retained. No code download URLs requested.

documentation.finding: Condition key names are case-insensitive; case-distinct resource tag keys can produce unexpected condition failures when only one value matches.

ResourceTag and RequestTag classified single-valued; AWS advises not using set operators on them. TagKeys is multivalued. Captured set-operator behavior is empirical, not recommended policy construction.
StringEquals compares values case-sensitively. ForAllValues requires every context value to match; ForAnyValue requires at least one. Negated set operators are captured separately.

main_matrix.same_session_initial_settled_agreement: 56/56 cases, including TagKeys controls; smallest settled session age 35.503 seconds

findings.order_controls: For Case/case, the value attached to case wins for both ResourceTag and RequestTag, independent of signed request insertion order and policy key spelling. Swapping value bindings swaps the allowed policy value. For CaSe/cASe without an exact lowercase key, ResourceTag instead selects the CaSe value while RequestTag selects the cASe value, again independent of insertion order and policy key spelling.
findings.interpretation: Observed main-matrix behavior is singleton selection, not aggregation of both case-distinct values. IAM internal context is not visible. The different mixed-case winners prohibit inferring a universal insertion-last, lexical-last, or exact-lowercase-preference rule from these captures. Native AWS does not document a stable collision winner; do not generalize a map-resolution algorithm beyond the observed keys/actions.
findings.atomicity: All 100 measured request-tag writes have root before/after readbacks consistent with authorization: denied writes preserve both prior values; allowed writes preserve two distinct tag keys with requested values.
findings.limitations: Only Lambda ListTags and TagResource on unqualified functions are measured. Set operators on ResourceTag/RequestTag were accepted and measured, but AWS documentation classifies these keys as single-valued and advises against set operators. The initial failed signing attempt and execution-role propagation error are retained separately, not treated as condition results.
